memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread; for seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in that month you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed." - Exodus 23:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The first festival called Israel to remember their deliverance from Egypt. Every year they would eat bread without yeast, just as they had on the night God rescued them in haste. It was a living memory, a way of never forgetting the day the Lord broke their chains and led them to freedom. God wanted His salvation kept fresh in their hearts, generation after generation.

There is deep wisdom in this. We are forgetful people. The mercies that once overwhelmed us with gratitude can fade into distant memory if we do not deliberately remember them. So God built remembrance into the rhythm of the year. He knew that a people who forgot their rescue would soon forget their Rescuer. Remembering was not mere nostalgia; it was the fuel of ongoing faith and thankfulness.

For us who follow Christ, this points beautifully to our own deliverance. Just as Israel was freed from Egypt, we have been freed from the far greater slavery of sin through Jesus, our Passover Lamb (1 Cor 5:7). And Jesus gave us our own way of remembering — the Lord's Supper, the bread and the cup, so that we would never forget the night He gave Himself for us. Take time today to remember how He saved you. Let the memory renew your gratitude and your love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I regularly remember and give thanks for how God has saved me?
How can I keep the memory of Christ's deliverance fresh in my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep the memory of Your salvation fresh in my heart. Thank You that in Christ, my Passover Lamb, I have been set free. May I never forget my Rescuer. Amen.
